name: Hand-Drawn Stop-Motion Style
visualIdentity: Drawn paper assets, clear lines, and a limited palette. Replacements and repositioning happen between held frames, with restrained, reproducible drawing variations. This is a simulated treatment; the style does not establish physical stop-motion photography.
suitableUses: Explicitly suited to short, charming loops. By inference, also fits illustrated explainers, craft tutorials, recipe videos, music-led social loops, and interactive stories where discrete visual states aid comprehension.
limitations: Held poses and deliberate replacement define the cadence; do not automatically smooth it with interpolated poses, bounce, or random jitter. Long hand-lettered copy is unsuitable. Gaze tracking requires readable eyes and appropriate layers or a rig; chapter transitions need meaningful boundaries and must not obscure causal links or violate continuous-shot or loop requirements.
palette: For new artwork only when no approved palette exists, suggested tokens are background #F7EEDD, foreground #344344, accent 1 #B6785D, accent 2 #819B81. These are suggestions, not canonical colors. Preserve supplied colors, roles, source artwork, and family/count limits. Use discrete colors; gradients are disabled. Accent 1/background text contrast is 3.125:1 and accent 2/foreground is 3.414:1, both below the 4.5:1 normal-text target; use accents decoratively and verify actual compositing.
motionAndInteraction: Preserve anticipation, weight, and settling with authored trajectories and held poses; distinguish drawing exposure rate from delivery frame rate. Seed and cache variants, evaluate from shared seekable time, and verify direct, backward, and out-of-order seeks. Interactive HTML may map finite scroll progress to reversible chapter or story states with reading holds; gaze following is optional, bounded character animation, not viewer tracking.
audio: No fixed soundtrack or mandatory layer is specified. Choose music, narration, vocals, effects, ambience, or silence for the subject and audience; honor supplied choices, synchronize to motion and reading holds, and keep speech clear. No audio assets are specified.
assetRequirements: Requires prepared drawing layers or numbered frames with transparency, consistent dimensions, and clear names. Inspect assets before composition. Rough.js can make seeded sketch-like contours, but does not supply handwriting, brush simulation, paper texture, poses, or authored drawing order. Additional facial motion needs suitable artwork or a rig.
combinations: Hand-lettered labels and arrows (style-024) can share drawing holds for craft, recipe, or personal-brand stories; keep copy short and variations reproducible. Beat-table timing (style-105) suits lyric-free music videos, jingles, and loops; retain reading pauses and avoid changing every element on every beat. Optional story, chapter, or gaze patterns require scene-supported assets and must respect the hand-drawn cadence.
productionApproach: Choose the visual renderer and motion method for the artwork and action; Canvas 2D is recommended, with PixiJS and Rough.js optional. HyperFrames is the primary composition, timing, sync, validation, and export pipeline; use Remotion only if unavailable or a verified required capability is missing, recording the reason. Keep rendering and motion logic separate from the pipeline; synchronize authorized audio, inspect representative frames and the decoded result, and deliver source, contact sheet, parameters, and reproducible instructions.
